A conventional coupon bond pays specified interest and principal; other instruments can have different structures. The coupon rate is applied to face value. The market price is what an investor pays or receives in a transaction. Yield relates price to the promised cash flows under stated assumptions. For a fixed stream of promised cash flows, a higher required yield generally means a lower price. This is why existing fixed-rate bonds can lose market value when interest rates rise, even if the issuer keeps paying. Holding to maturity does not eliminate default or reinvestment risk, and investors needing to sell early face market conditions. Invented Rs 1,000 face-value bond pays Rs 80 annual coupon. Bought at Rs 950, its current yield is 80 / 950, about 8.42%. That is not automatically its yield to maturity, which also depends on redemption, remaining tenor and timing. Bought at a different price, the same coupon does not produce the same investor return. Compare issuer, maturity, coupon structure, credit ranking, collateral and liquidity before choosing a product. 'Fixed income' does not mean market value is fixed or repayment guaranteed. The objective trap is often to substitute a familiar deposit concept for a traded security. The descriptive task is to explain both the funding benefit for issuers and risk allocation to investors.

teaching_notes.title: 2. CP, NCD, securitisation, security receipts and MLDs
paragraphs: Commercial paper is a short-term funding instrument for eligible issuers. A non-convertible debenture is debt without the specified equity-conversion feature. Securitised debt is supported by cash flows from a pool of financial assets. A security receipt is associated with an asset-reconstruction arrangement and the acquired financial assets under that framework. A market-linked debenture links its contractual payoff to a defined market variable.

The common word 'debt' does not make these instruments economically identical. For securitisation, evaluate the underlying pool, structure and protections. For security receipts, realisation from stressed assets matters. For an MLD, understand both issuer credit risk and payoff conditions; a market-linked return does not automatically confer ownership in the linked equity index.

Invented pool contains many vehicle loans in the same region and industry. Having many loans can diversify individual borrower risk but may leave a shared economic-shock exposure. Pooling does not turn weak loans into risk-free assets. Similarly, a high promised return on distressed recoveries reflects risk and uncertainty, not a free yield improvement.

Prepare comparisons by issuer, tenor, underlying cash flow, liquidity and investor claim. Avoid memorising long instrument lists without one usable example each. The October framework's claimed applicability to these instruments remains unverified; instrument definitions are being taught as financial concepts, not as confirmation of an operative new disclosure circular.

teaching_notes.title: 3. Credit risk, interest-rate risk and liquidity risk
paragraphs: Credit risk concerns failure to meet promised obligations. Interest-rate risk concerns changes in value when required rates change. Liquidity risk concerns the ability to transact promptly without an unacceptable price concession, or to obtain funding when due. A single instrument can carry all three. A credit rating addresses a credit assessment, not the investor's entire risk picture.

Collateral or secured status can improve recovery prospects, depending on enforceability, value and priority. It does not guarantee full or immediate repayment. The asset may fall in value, already support other claims or take time to realise. Unsecured status means no specified collateral backing of that type, not automatically immediate default.

Invented highly rated long-duration bond experiences a market-price fall after yields rise. That does not necessarily mean its issuer was downgraded. Another bond may retain a stable indicative price but be difficult to sell because few buyers exist. Looking only at rating or last-traded price can therefore miss important risk.

In an FM answer, match controls to risks: credit appraisal and diversification for credit exposure, duration/hedging choices for rate exposure and liquidity buffers or market access for trading/funding needs. Each control leaves residual risk. Do not claim that a risk meter, exchange listing, collateral or digital platform replaces a full assessment of the investor's horizon and need for cash.

teaching_notes.title: 4. Credit Risk-o-Meter: disclosure logic and rating changes
paragraphs: The reported Credit Risk-o-Meter translates credit-rating information into a simpler visual display. The policy rationale is to make a difficult symbol system more understandable at the point of choice. Simplification helps only if the investor sees its limited meaning: a display of credit risk is not a personalised recommendation or a measure of every market and liquidity risk.

The compilation reports six categories, identification of the CRA and actual rating, an unsecured warning, use of the lowest rating where there are multiple ratings and explicit Issuer Not Cooperating status. INC signals an information/cooperation concern; it should not be casually treated as an ordinary strong rating or automatically equated with an adjudicated fraud finding.

For an invented security rated differently by two agencies, a conservative display avoids selecting only the more favourable assessment. Explain the rating's date and updates. A rating can change as new information emerges, and delayed platform updates can mislead buyers even if the original display was correct.

The reported 24-hour OBPP update rule, effective date and exact rating-category mapping require verification. Do not invent colours from a text extraction or memorise the file's categories as authenticated law. Learn the disclosure mechanism, its scope and residual limitations. The exam trap is often an absolute statement such as 'lowest-risk display guarantees capital protection' or 'the meter assesses suitability for all investors'.

teaching_notes.title: 5. AT1 and perpetual bonds: risks beyond an ordinary bond label
paragraphs: AT1 instruments can help eligible banks meet the Additional Tier 1 capital layer. Their terms include special loss-absorption and distribution features under the applicable framework. These features make them materially different from an ordinary senior fixed-maturity bond or a deposit, even if both products display an interest rate.

Perpetual means there is no ordinary fixed maturity date at which principal must be repaid in the same way as a conventional term bond. A call option gives the issuer a conditional ability to redeem under its terms; it is not an investor's guaranteed repayment date. Investors should not automatically value the instrument as though the first possible call must occur.

Invented investor needs all funds back in five years but buys a perpetual bank instrument because a salesperson mentions a five-year call. If the call is not exercised or losses are absorbed under the terms, the investor's planned cash availability can fail. A familiar bank name and periodic coupon do not remove this mismatch.

The October risk-display discussion explicitly warns that a visual credit scale may not capture every AT1 feature. For exam preparation, retain the distinctions: capital instrument versus deposit, call versus maturity and credit assessment versus contractual loss absorption. Do not give the broad advice that all bank bonds are safe because banks are regulated.

teaching_notes.title: 1. Issuance size versus secondary-market depth
paragraphs: A corporate-bond market can grow in outstanding stock without becoming easy to trade. Outstanding debt measures accumulated securities remaining in issue; turnover measures trading activity over a period. A large stock held to maturity by a narrow investor base can coexist with thin secondary liquidity and poor price discovery.

Companies can use bonds to diversify funding beyond bank loans and better match long-lived projects with longer-term finance. But access may remain concentrated among stronger issuers. Broad market growth does not establish that small or lower-rated firms can raise funds on reasonable terms, or that retail investors can exit cheaply.

Invented market doubles outstanding bonds while daily trading stays unchanged. Its stock has grown, but turnover relative to outstanding debt has fallen. Investors who need to sell may still face a wide bid-ask spread. Do not infer liquidity from a headline market-size number or from the fact that a security is listed.

The file gives nearby market-size observations around Rs 61 trillion/lakh-crore-equivalent descriptions with different reference dates/rounding. Keep units and dates attached; do not manufacture a precise time series by treating them as identical measurements. Reform analysis should identify the bottleneck: issuance, information, distribution, hedging, market making or settlement. Different tools address different bottlenecks and do not substitute for each other.

teaching_notes.title: 2. OBPP and FICP: access, distribution and investor protection
paragraphs: An Online Bond Platform Provider offers a digital route to discover and transact in eligible debt securities under its regulatory framework. The investor may compare maturity, yield, rating, price and minimum amount, complete KYC, place an order and receive servicing. The platform is an intermediary; the bond's issuer remains responsible for its promised payments under the terms.

Registration and a usable interface do not guarantee product quality, market liquidity or personalised suitability. Investors still need transparent charges, accurate disclosures, safe payment/settlement arrangements and grievance handling. A high displayed yield may reflect credit or liquidity risk, not superior risk-free income.

The file describes PB Money and its operating/parent entities as a newly authorised platform. The authorisation and corporate details remain unverified. It also describes Fixed Income Channel Partners as a proposed distribution layer through regulated OBPPs, with limits on handling client assets and charging investors. A proposed distributor model is not proof that every financial agent can now distribute every bond.

Invented distributor explains bond choices in a smaller town but asks the investor to transfer funds to a personal account. That request should not be legitimised by the mere use of an official-sounding acronym. For the exam, learn who provides access, who issues the security, who keeps the ownership record and which safeguards must remain in the transaction chain.

teaching_notes.title: 3. Bond-index futures and basis risk
paragraphs: A corporate-bond index summarises a specified basket's performance. A futures contract linked to that index allows exposure to changes in the index under its terms. A bond investor concerned about a fall in the relevant market value may use an appropriate short hedge. The precise quantity and contract choice depend on how the portfolio responds relative to the index.

Basis risk arises because the actual portfolio and the hedge do not move in perfectly offsetting ways. They may differ in duration, credit composition, liquidity or constituents. A hedge against broad rate movements does not ensure recovery after one issuer defaults. Margin requirements can also generate short-term funding needs.

Invented portfolio loses Rs 5 lakh while its short futures position gains Rs 4 lakh. The hedge reduced loss to Rs 1 lakh before costs, but did not eliminate it. If the portfolio instead rises, the hedge may reduce the upside. This does not automatically make it a failed hedge; the objective was risk reduction rather than winning on both sides.

The article reports an NSE no-objection certificate and a further RBI approval requirement. An NOC is not the same as final operational launch, contract liquidity or permission for every investor category. Learn the lifecycle: proposal, regulatory steps, product specification, launch and actual adoption. Do not describe a future product as already widely traded.

teaching_notes.title: 4. Market makers, spreads, inventory and repo funding
paragraphs: A market maker supplies buy and sell quotes under the relevant arrangement and may hold inventory to facilitate transactions. The bid-ask spread partly compensates for inventory, adverse-selection, funding and operating risks. Regular quotes can improve trade execution and price discovery without guaranteeing that every investor can transact at the price they prefer.

Inventory exposes the intermediary to price changes while it waits to offset positions. Repo access can provide funding against securities and help manage liquidity, but it does not remove credit, collateral-valuation or funding-rollover risk. A securities-financing facility is not free capital or a government guarantee of bond prices.

Invented bond is quoted at 99 bid and 101 ask per Rs 100 face. An immediate buyer pays around the ask and an immediate seller receives around the bid, subject to size and conditions. The spread is a transaction cost. If conditions deteriorate, quotes may widen or available size shrink; a framework cannot be assessed only by whether a market maker is named.

The October market-making and distribution initiatives have different legal stages, including proposals. Keep that status explicit. For descriptive preparation, assess success through sustained quote quality, turnover, participation and orderly stress performance. Avoid treating growing issuance alone as evidence that the market-making problem is solved.

teaching_notes.title: 5. Tokenisation, DLT, smart contracts and atomic settlement
paragraphs: Tokenisation represents a specified asset or right through a digital token. Distributed ledger technology changes how records may be shared and updated; it does not automatically change the legal obligation of the bond issuer. A tokenised claim still requires clarity about ownership, enforceability, servicing and what happens if the technology fails.

Atomic settlement links the transfer of the asset and payment so the intended exchange occurs together under the mechanism. This can reduce principal settlement risk: one party delivering the security while the other fails to pay. It does not eliminate issuer default, adverse price movements, mistaken instructions or cyber risk.

Invented investor buys a bond for Rs 10 lakh. A linked settlement process transfers both the security claim and payment under agreed conditions. A smart contract can automate a coupon event, but only if the issuer has funded it and the coded conditions correctly reflect the legal terms. Automation cannot create money when the issuer is insolvent.

The file reports a Demat 2.0 pilot connected to wholesale CBDC through a specified interface, with initial issuers and amounts. These claims are unverified. Wholesale settlement between eligible participants is not the same use case as retail programmable e-rupee spending restrictions. Learn benefits, governance, interoperability, legal finality and residual risks; do not equate tokenisation with an unbacked cryptocurrency or proof of universally faster, safer markets.

cards.answer: Worked answer: Investor education helps people understand product features, risks, costs and basic rights. It is not the same service as personalised investment advice. A general awareness message cannot determine whether a particular bond or derivative fits an individual's cash-flow needs, experience and risk capacity. The October file describes Project Jagrook as an umbrella awareness initiative, Samajh Se Investing Simple as a campaign and MUST as a trainer-based student outreach model. These are reported programme details, not independently authenticated launches. The conceptual hierarchy matters: a broad project, a specific campaign and a delivery mechanism can coexist without being three unrelated regulators. Placing messages where trading decisions occur can reduce the gap between classroom awareness and actual behaviour. Yet repetitive warnings may be ignored, jargon can exclude beginners and a warning alone cannot counter aggressive sales incentives. Effective education uses understandable examples, verifies comprehension and supports safe actions rather than merely counting impressions. Invented student sees a promised 'guaranteed daily return'. Useful literacy means identifying the inconsistency, checking the regulated entity and payment destination through authentic channels and understanding that registration is not a return guarantee. teaching_notes.title: 2. SEBI, IOSCO, NISM, exchanges, depositories and AMFI
paragraphs: SEBI regulates the securities market within its mandate. IOSCO is an international cooperation/standards forum for securities regulators, not the operator of every Indian trade. NISM supports securities-market education, training and certification. AMFI represents the mutual-fund industry and supports industry standards and awareness; it is not a substitute statutory regulator for all investments.

An exchange facilitates trading under its rules. A depository maintains electronic records of securities holdings through the relevant participant structure. Clearing and settlement determine and discharge obligations. These stages are connected, but an order placed through a broker is not the same event as final credit of securities to the investor's account.

Invented investor buys shares through a broker on an exchange. The exchange provides the matching/trading mechanism, while the ownership record is maintained through the depository arrangement after settlement. Calling the depository a stock exchange misidentifies the function. Calling the broker the issuer also confuses an intermediary with the company whose shares are traded.

For efficient recall, use institution -> function -> example -> not-this-function. This is more resilient to application MCQs than memorising headquarters and taglines alone. The campaigns in the October file involve several market partners; partnership in education does not collapse their mandates into one. Keep unverified event participation separate from the durable institutional roles.

teaching_notes.title: 3. AI surveillance: filings, trade data, fraud content and audit
paragraphs: Surveillance searches for patterns that warrant attention. Corporate-filing analysis can examine unusual accounting relationships or changes across periods; trading surveillance examines transactions and market behaviour. These are different datasets and risks. An anomalous number may reflect a legitimate business change, a data error or misconduct, so an alert requires investigation.

The file reports a corporate-fraud model under development and names Sudarsan for social-media fraud content, R(AI)DAR for advertisements, InfoMerge for investigative support and C-SAC for cyber-audit processes. The names, deployment status and claimed counts remain unverified. Learn the function mapping without promoting a planned model to universal live operation.

Invented company reports sharply rising revenue while receivables and cash conversion deteriorate. A model flags the pattern. Investigators then examine contracts, collections, related parties and accounting explanations. The model has prioritised a case; it has not established fraud or imposed a lawful penalty. Equally, a model failing to flag a case does not certify that the filing is truthful.

AI can expand coverage and speed analysis, but creates model, data, privacy and explainability risks. Good governance includes validated inputs, testing, monitoring, human accountability and due process. A descriptive answer should compare capability with limitations instead of repeating the false dichotomy that all earlier supervision was complaint-only and AI automatically prevents every violation.

teaching_notes.title: 4. Brand promotion versus product inducement
paragraphs: Financial advertising can influence decisions before an investor reads the technical disclosures. A celebrity's visibility may create an impression of safety or quality unrelated to the product's actual risk. The key distinction is between promoting an entity's brand and making a specific claim that induces investment in a particular product or service.

The file reports a Common Advertisement Code, special approval for celebrity advertisements and restrictions on passing endorsement costs to clients or mutual-fund schemes. These legal details need authentication. Do not assume a reported move toward post-issuance reporting means every advertisement, including special cases, is free from prior checks.

Invented advertisement says a famous person uses Platform X. Another says 'Buy Bond Y for a guaranteed superior return'. The second contains a product/outcome claim that requires very different scrutiny. Neither a celebrity appearance nor platform registration demonstrates that the investment is suitable for a particular customer.

For an FM or ethics answer, explain clear and balanced communication, conflicts of interest, substantiation of claims and cost transparency. A disclaimer in tiny text should not be used to neutralise a misleading headline. The desired outcome is informed choice, not merely formal compliance with an advertisement checklist. Do not treat all marketing as prohibited or all brand promotion as endorsement of every product on the platform.

teaching_notes.title: 5. Ratings, rankings, past returns and verified claims
paragraphs: A ranking is meaningful only within a defined category, method and period. 'Number one' could refer to client count, an award, survey responses or a selected performance measure. Without a denominator and methodology, the comparison can be persuasive but uninformative. Past return claims also depend on fees, risk, survivorship and the selected start/end dates.

The compilation refers to PaRRVA in the context of verifying past risk-return claims and eligible ratings/rankings. Treat the described legal permissions as unverified. The general principle is that substantiated historical information can improve transparency without proving future performance or investor suitability.

Invented fund A reports a higher three-year return than fund B but took much greater credit risk and holds illiquid assets. A return-only advertisement omits information needed for a fair comparison. Similarly, an award based on only three voluntary survey participants should not be presented as a census of the entire market.

For objective preparation, ask who made the claim, what was measured, which peer group and period were used and what limitations were disclosed. For descriptive preparation, connect truthful communication to trust and market development. Do not conclude that a verified past performance claim, a high rating or a broad campaign has removed the investor's need to assess costs, risk and time horizon.

teaching_notes.title: 1. Closing auction and price discovery
paragraphs: A closing auction collects eligible orders in a defined end-of-day process to establish the closing price under exchange rules. Continuous trading matches orders during the session; an auction aggregates interest at a dedicated point. The objective is a robust reference price, not a guarantee that every pending order executes.

An order-entry window can have stages with different permitted order types. Randomised closure can reduce the ability to time a last-instant change with certainty. It does not eliminate manipulation risk by itself: surveillance, transparent rules, appropriate participation and system controls still matter.

Invented investor submits a buy limit of Rs 100 while the auction clears at Rs 102. The existence of a closing auction does not force the investor to pay above the limit or guarantee that the order fills. An order expresses willingness under conditions; the auction must apply the actual matching and allocation rules.

The file reports a revised 3:30-3:40 PM framework and later implementation dates. Those operational details require authentication and must not be used as live trading instructions. For FM, learn purpose, process and limitations. Distinguish the Closing Auction Session from the Consolidated Account Statement in AA-related news; the same acronym does not imply the same function.

teaching_notes.title: 2. VWAP and derivative settlement prices
paragraphs: Volume-Weighted Average Price equals total traded value divided by total traded quantity over the specified set of trades. It gives larger quantities more influence. It is not the simple mean of quoted prices unless quantities happen to be equal, and it cannot be computed reliably from prices without the associated volumes.

Invented trades: 100 shares at Rs 100 and 300 at Rs 104. Total value is Rs 41,200 and quantity 400, giving VWAP Rs 103. The simple average of the two prices would be Rs 102 and is wrong for this volume-weighted calculation. State the time window and eligible trade set; a day's VWAP and a last-30-minute VWAP can differ.

A derivative's final settlement uses the reference specified in its rules. The official auction closing price of the underlying need not be that same reference. The supplied CAS article explicitly distinguishes closing-price discovery from the reported 30-minute VWAP treatment for expiring derivatives; the operative rule and dates are not authenticated here.

Invented share closes in auction at Rs 105 while its defined continuous-trading VWAP is Rs 103. If a hypothetical contract prescribes the latter, use Rs 103 rather than the visually prominent closing quote. For index derivatives, follow the specified index methodology; do not casually average constituent prices. This is a rule-application skill, not permission to assume every market uses identical settlement methods.

teaching_notes.title: 3. Limit, market, stop-loss and iceberg orders
paragraphs: A limit order sets a maximum purchase price or minimum sale price. It controls price but does not guarantee execution. A market order seeks execution at available market prices under the venue's rules and can face slippage. A stop-loss order activates when its trigger condition is met; it is not a guaranteed sale at the trigger price in every market condition.

An iceberg order displays only a part of a larger quantity through the relevant mechanism. Display rules do not change the investor's total intended quantity. An auction may treat existing or new orders differently from continuous trading. Carry-forward of a limit order, conversion of displayed quantities or exclusion of stop orders requires the actual applicable rules.

Invented seller sets a Rs 98 limit while the market gaps to Rs 95. The order may remain unfilled rather than execute at Rs 98. A stop trigger at Rs 98 can activate a subsequent order, but the eventual execution depends on its type and available prices. Labelling an order 'protective' does not remove liquidity risk.

The October file gives specific CAS carry-forward and order-entry changes with separate commencement dates. Keep them unverified. Study the order features and the question's assumed rules first, then apply those assumptions exactly. Do not infer that every pending order automatically migrates to the auction or that an unexecuted order has already created a completed trade.

teaching_notes.title: 4. IPO: fresh issue, offer for sale and disclosure documents
paragraphs: An IPO can include newly issued shares, shares sold by existing holders or both. Fresh-issue proceeds go to the issuer under the issue structure. Offer-for-sale proceeds go to selling shareholders. Buying shares in an IPO does not prove that the entire amount finances a new factory or expands the issuer's cash balance.

The Draft Red Herring Prospectus is part of the issue-disclosure process. It explains the business, financials, risks and proposed use of funds under applicable requirements. Updates or addenda communicate material changes. Regulatory review is not an investment recommendation or a guarantee of future share-price performance.

Invented IPO raises Rs 1,000 crore through a fresh issue and Rs 500 crore through selling shareholders. The company receives the fresh component, subject to costs and structure, not the full Rs 1,500 crore as business capital. If market conditions change, the issuer may need to revise the funding plan and disclosures.

For exam preparation, connect primary issuance to capital formation and secondary sales to ownership/liquidity. Both can occur at a public offering. Do not equate public subscription, stock-exchange listing and risk-free investment. Merchant bankers coordinate and perform specified due diligence; they do not become guarantors of the issuer's business success simply by managing the issue.

teaching_notes.title: 5. Temporary fresh-issue flexibility: percentage base and conditions
paragraphs: The file reports temporary flexibility to revise the fresh-issue size by up to 50% without a fresh draft filing, subject to conditions and an issue-opening cutoff. This is an unverified regulatory change. Its conceptual structure is limited relief from one process requirement, not a waiver of all disclosures or permission to change the fundamental object without scrutiny.

Invented original fresh issue is Rs 800 crore. A hypothetical symmetric 25% tolerance would permit a range from Rs 600 crore to Rs 1,000 crore if all other conditions were met. The percentage is applied to the defined original fresh component, not automatically to the combined fresh issue plus OFS or to the company's market capitalisation.

Retaining the main objective matters because investors need to know why funds are being raised. If a project is reduced or financing changes, updated disclosures should explain the effect. A lead manager's responsibility and public addendum are safeguards, not optional decorations.

Keep the publication date, extension date, eligibility based on IPO opening and end of temporary relief separate. An announced extension is not a permanent replacement of the standard framework. For GA, retain the rule only after official verification; for FM, explain the trade-off between flexibility in volatile markets and investors receiving accurate, comparable information before deciding.

cards.question: Explain the first study target, give an example and state one misleading inference.
cards.answer: Worked answer: A loan is an asset of the lender because it represents expected future cash receipts. It is a liability of the borrower. A non-performing classification identifies specified repayment problems under the applicable prudential framework. A familiar term-loan overdue benchmark should not be mechanically extended to every product or every institution without checking the rules. Gross NPAs are the classified problem-loan amount before the specified adjustments. The GNPA ratio compares that amount with gross advances on the same measurement basis. Invented NBFC has Rs 24 crore gross NPAs and Rs 1,000 crore gross advances: GNPA ratio = 2.4%. This means a measured share of loans is classified non-performing; it is not a 2.4% probability that every borrower defaults tomorrow. A ratio can improve through recovery, write-off, reclassification or denominator growth. If problem loans remain Rs 24 crore while gross advances grow to Rs 1,200 crore, the ratio falls to 2% without a reduction in the problem-loan stock. That may still be useful information, but it does not prove cash recovery improved. The file reports a historical decline in NBFC GNPA and current sector figures. Those observations are unverified and not a complete time series. For FM/GA, learn the formula, units, reference period and comparison base. Do not equate a write-off with a borrower necessarily being forgiven, or classify a lower ratio as sufficient evidence that all risk has fallen.

teaching_notes.title: 2. Sector concentration, weighted risk and systemic linkages
paragraphs: A sector can have a high default ratio but a small share of the loan book. Its contribution to total problem loans depends on both. Conversely, a moderate ratio in a very large lending segment can produce a large absolute problem-loan stock. Rankings by stress rate and rankings by contribution need not match.

Invented lender has Rs 1,000 crore loans, of which 2% is agriculture. At a hypothetical agriculture GNPA of 6%, that segment contributes Rs 1.2 crore gross NPAs: 1,000 x 2% x 6%. If a Rs 500 crore retail segment has 3% GNPA, it contributes Rs 15 crore. The agriculture rate is higher, but its absolute contribution is lower.

NBFCs can widen credit access and specialise in particular markets. They can also transmit stress through bank borrowing, market funding, common borrowers and shared collateral. Asset quality is only one dimension: funding maturity, liquidity, capital and governance matter too. A strong GNPA figure does not prove that refinancing risk is small.

The supplied FSR notes also discuss microfinance multiple borrowing, outreach and NBFC retail credit. Use these as complementary source-era context, not independent validation of every October number. In an answer, assess disaggregated lending, borrower resilience and funding links. Do not infer that stronger aggregate asset quality means every NBFC, sector or household has improved.

teaching_notes.title: 3. UPI, NPCI, banks, P2P and P2M
paragraphs: UPI is an interoperable payment arrangement operated by NPCI within the regulatory ecosystem. A user's app provides an interface while participating banks hold relevant accounts and perform their roles in the payment chain. The app brand, the underlying bank and the system operator are not automatically the same legal entity.

P2P is person-to-person, such as transferring money to a friend. P2M is a payment to a merchant for a good or service. A merchant accepting payment is not thereby a bank, and a payment app is not automatically authorised to take deposits or lend on its own balance sheet.

Invented customer pays Rs 5,000 to a shop using a bank-account-linked interface. The visible app initiates the interaction, but interbank obligations and settlement follow the system's arrangements. Faster user confirmation does not mean there are no operational, fraud or settlement controls behind the interface.

For FM, explain the benefits of convenient, interoperable payments alongside access, grievance, fraud and continuity issues. For GA, match NPCI to its payment-system role without calling it the monetary-policy authority. Do not use the payment channel's name alone to infer a fee: instrument, transaction type and the applicable legal/payment framework can matter. The October fee story does not authenticate a universal charge.

teaching_notes.title: 4. MDR, caps, thresholds and the verification hold
paragraphs: Merchant Discount Rate is a processing-related fee generally borne by the merchant under the relevant payment arrangement. It is not automatically a fee charged directly to the payer's bank account. Interchange, platform charges and customer charges are distinct concepts; one cannot substitute a figure from one category for another without checking the framework.

For arithmetic only, assume a hypothetical 0.5% merchant fee capped at Rs 200 and a qualifying payment of Rs 60,000. The percentage gives Rs 300, but the cap makes the fee Rs 200. This is an invented rule for studying caps, not a statement that any such UPI charge is operative.

A threshold can decide eligibility without being a deduction from the chargeable amount. If a hypothetical rule applies to qualifying transactions above X, do not assume the fee applies only to the excess above X unless specified. Likewise, a postponement is not cancellation; a future date to be announced is not a precise commencement date.

The October file's 0.4%, Rs 2,000 threshold, Rs 300 cap and post-Diwali timing are on verification hold. Do not advise merchants or customers to pay these amounts based on this library. Study the rate-base-cap-payer-scope checklist and verify any real policy through authentic official releases before treating it as a memorisation fact or operational instruction.

teaching_notes.title: 1. GST Council, officers' committee and GSTN
paragraphs: The GST Council is the constitutional body under Article 279A for recommendations on specified GST matters. It brings Union and State perspectives into a shared indirect-tax framework. A meeting recommendation, an enacted amendment and an operative notification are different legal stages. The Council's recommendation cannot be treated as sufficient evidence that a taxpayer's obligation already changed.

An officers' committee examines technical or implementation issues and prepares suggestions. GSTN supports technology and information processes. Neither should be described as replacing the Council or unilaterally rewriting constitutional and statutory arrangements. A portal automating a process does not itself create legal authority for a new tax.

The October file proposes a Standing Committee with 12 state representatives, five named permanent positions and rotation for the rest. The structure and names remain unverified. Learn the coordination logic: consolidate technical work, reduce duplication and bring implementation problems to the appropriate decision-making authority. Do not imply that states outside a technical committee lose all constitutional participation.

Invented problem: businesses cannot correctly amend a registration field. Officers examine the form, GSTN evaluates the software change and the competent authority implements any required legal/procedural change. These actors solve different parts of the problem. A useful answer separates policy, administration, technology and taxpayer rights instead of calling every institution 'the GST regulator'.

teaching_notes.title: 2. Input tax credit and invoice reconciliation
paragraphs: Input Tax Credit allows eligible tax paid on business inputs to offset specified output tax liability, subject to the law's conditions. The mechanism reduces cascading when credit flows appropriately. It is not a blanket refund of every business expense, and claiming credit requires more than the buyer simply wishing to reduce tax.

Invented business has Rs 180 output GST and Rs 100 eligible input credit with no other complications. The simple net cash requirement is Rs 80. If only Rs 70 is eligible, the result becomes Rs 110. A purchase carrying tax does not automatically make all of that tax claimable under every circumstance.

Supplier reporting, recipient records and relevant electronic statements need reconciliation. An invoice-management facility can help accept, reject or review records. Differences can arise from timing, errors or fraud; a mismatch is a signal to examine, not proof in itself of deliberate evasion. Reversed credit and later reclaimed credit also need a clear trail to avoid double counting.

The October return-reform proposals and start periods are not authenticated. Learn sales/outward reporting, summary liability and eligible input-credit information as connected but distinct records. For FM/ESI, explain how better matching can reduce leakage and disputes, while poor implementation can raise compliance costs and interrupt working capital. Automation must support accurate entitlements and correction procedures.

teaching_notes.title: 3. Cash ledger, credit ledger, refunds and inverted duty
paragraphs: A cash ledger records deposited money available for the relevant tax payments. A credit ledger records eligible ITC under the framework. The ability to use credit is not identical to an unrestricted right to withdraw cash. Refund eligibility, documentation, adjustment of dues and timing are separate questions.

An inverted duty structure arises when relevant input tax rates exceed output rates, potentially accumulating unused ITC. Zero-rated supplies have their own treatment and eligible credit/refund mechanisms under the law. Zero-rated and exempt should not be used as synonyms: treatment of input credit can differ. Nor should one assume every exporter always uses the same procedural route.

Invented business has Rs 120 eligible input tax and Rs 60 output liability. Unused credit of Rs 60 may remain, but whether and how it can be refunded depends on the applicable category and rules. Delayed eligible refunds tie up funds the business could otherwise use for inventory or payroll, creating a financing cost.

The file reports phased automation, a 90% provisional amount in specified cases and shorter processing steps. These remain recommendations/claims pending verification. A provisional refund is not necessarily a final approval; risk-based processing is not a waiver of valid checks. In an answer, balance faster working-capital release with fraud prevention, transparent reasons for withholding and timely correction/grievance routes.

teaching_notes.title: 4. Reverse charge, TDS, e-invoicing and the tax base
paragraphs: Under reverse charge, the specified recipient rather than the ordinary supplier remits the tax under the relevant rule. It changes responsibility for payment; it does not necessarily mean the transaction is tax-free. Eligibility for related input credit is another legal question. Tax deducted at source is a collection/withholding mechanism, not automatically the final tax rate on the supply.

Electronic invoicing uses prescribed structured reporting and identification processes; it is not merely sending a PDF invoice by email. Extending digital records can support matching and identify under-reporting, but requires clear scope, reliable systems and proportionate compliance costs. B2B and B2C refer to different transaction relationships and should not be interchanged.

Invented shop records only half its consumer sales. Better transaction data may reveal a discrepancy, but tax authorities must still apply the law, check explanations and protect data. The presence of an analytics flag does not determine final liability. Registration, return reporting, invoice generation and payment are separate compliance steps.

The October proposals include e-invoicing, specified scrap transactions and tools for expanding the GST base. Their exact thresholds and rates remain unverified. 'Expanding the base' should mean bringing legally liable activity into proper compliance, not arbitrarily taxing exempt persons. Distinguish a broader reported taxpayer count from improved accuracy, active filing and actual tax realisation.

teaching_notes.title: 5. Registration, small e-commerce sellers and return simplification
paragraphs: Registration identifies persons under the tax system; amendments maintain the accuracy of that record. Simplifying routine changes can reduce administrative friction, while sensitive changes such as a principal place of business may require different checks. Automatic processing is a workflow choice, not proof that all eligibility conditions cease to apply.

Small online sellers can face disproportionate burdens when supplying across jurisdictions. The file reports a simplified mechanism involving other-state registration and a monthly ITC-transfer condition. The specific Rs 2.5 lakh figure and eligibility are unverified. Do not turn the proposal into universal permission for every seller to dispense with any physical presence requirement.

Return frequency and tax-payment frequency need not be identical. A scheme can, in principle, combine an annual return with quarterly payments under specified conditions. That is not the same as paying tax only annually, or never keeping transaction records. The reported ARQP scheme and Rs 5 crore turnover condition require authentication.

Invented enterprise spends a large share of its staff time correcting repetitive portal fields. Better forms and consistent rules can reduce its compliance cost without reducing lawful tax liability. Evaluate simplification using time, error rates, access and effective safeguards. Do not assume every administrative relaxation is a tax exemption or that fewer forms necessarily means weaker enforcement.

teaching_notes.title: 6. Notices, penalties, appeal deposits and prosecution
paragraphs: Tax liability, interest and penalty have different purposes. A notice asks the taxpayer to respond to a proposed action; it is not the same as a final adjudication. An appeal pre-deposit is a procedural payment linked to pursuing a challenge, not automatically the final penalty or a waiver of the remaining dispute.

Invented penalty demand is Rs 100 crore and a hypothetical appeal rule caps the required deposit at Rs 20 crore. The cap does not reduce the final liability to Rs 20 crore or mean no further amount can be due after adjudication. Nor does paying a deposit prove that the taxpayer admits the entire demand.

Civil errors and deliberate fraud require appropriately differentiated treatment. Hearings, reasons and proportionate procedures support fairness and certainty. Criminal prosecution and arrest powers are especially consequential; do not infer their current existence or removal from a compilation's summary of a Council recommendation.

The file reports changes to small-notice thresholds, general penalties, early-payment relief, appeal caps and prosecution/arrest provisions. All specific legal changes require authentication and implementation evidence. Study the distinction and sequence first: detect issue, notify, allow response, determine liability, permit lawful appeal and apply the relevant enforcement route. Avoid learning a proposed monetary threshold without its offence, component, timing and legal stage.

teaching_notes.title: 7. Exports, SEZ/FTWZ, place of supply and movement of goods
paragraphs: A transaction involving an overseas customer is not automatically an export for every GST purpose. Definitions can require conditions involving supplier/recipient location, place of supply, payment and relationships between establishments. The place-of-supply rule identifies the relevant jurisdiction under the law; it is not simply wherever a salesperson happens to be located.

SEZs and Free Trade Warehousing Zones operate under specified frameworks. Their presence in a supply chain does not make every connected domestic transaction automatically zero-rated. The particular supply and authorised activities matter. Likewise, receipt in rupees or foreign currency must be assessed under the actual export conditions rather than a blanket assumption.

Invented Indian firm provides a service to a related overseas establishment. A commercial invoice and foreign address are not enough to settle every tax question. The correct analysis checks the law's conditions, including any treatment of establishments. The October article reports proposed relaxation/clarification; it does not prove that all such services now qualify.

Goods-movement reforms can reduce repeated checks and logistics delays while preserving targeted enforcement against real evasion. A policy discouraging routine transit interception is not a universal ban on lawful inspection. For ESI/FM, connect predictable administration to trade competitiveness, working capital and federal coordination. Keep proposed export and transit changes labelled as proposals until the required legal steps are verified.

teaching_notes.title: 8. Sector-specific GST proposals: classify the type of change
paragraphs: The sector list is best learned by the tax mechanism changed, not as an unstructured catalogue of rates. A lower rate changes output liability; an exemption can alter credit consequences; a margin scheme changes the taxable base; reverse charge changes the remitter; self-certification changes the evidence process. These are not interchangeable forms of 'GST relief'.

The October file groups proposals for agricultural inputs/services, selected scrap, used vehicles, EV transport, delivery platforms, specified helicopter travel, research institutions, shipping and highway arrangements. Every specific rate, coverage condition and exemption is unverified. The useful breadth layer is understanding why different sectors raise different compliance and valuation questions.

Invented used-goods dealer sells a repaired item. A margin-based rule might define tax on a specified margin instead of total selling price, while separately controlling credit on purchase and repair inputs. Permission for one expense does not imply unrestricted ITC on every cost. A research exemption also needs a definition separating genuine research from ordinary consultancy; a certificate is a process safeguard, not a magic label.

For exam preparation, retain one example of each mechanism and the key exception. Do not spend disproportionate time memorising every proposed niche classification before mastering Council authority, ITC and refunds. The revision table below provides the coverage checklist, while any exact rate must wait for an authenticated operative source.

teaching_notes.title: 1. Index level, YoY, MoM and percentage-point change
paragraphs: An index expresses a measured level relative to a base. If the base is 100 and the index is 120, the measured level is 20% above the base-period level under that series. It does not follow that growth in the latest month or year is 20%. Growth requires a comparison index from the relevant period.

Year-on-year change = (current index / same-month-last-year index - 1) x 100. Month-on-month change compares with the preceding month. Invented current index 120, previous month 118 and year-earlier month 110 gives YoY about 9.09% and MoM about 1.69%. The index-point increase from 118 to 120 is 2 points, not 2% growth.

If annual inflation moves from 5% to 6%, the change in the rate is 1 percentage point; the rate itself increased by 20% relative to 5%. An exam may ask any of these quantities. Write the denominator and unit explicitly before calculating.

The October tables contain index levels and annual rates alongside each other. Treat them as separate observations rather than subtracting one from the other. When a figure is provisional, label it accordingly. This skill transfers across CPI, WPI, PPI and IIP, but the economic meaning of the underlying index differs: prices are not the same variable as physical production volume.

teaching_notes.title: 2. CPI versus WPI versus Output PPI
paragraphs: CPI measures price changes for a specified household-consumption basket. WPI measures a specified wholesale-goods price basket. Output PPI concerns prices received by producers under the series' defined coverage. Different stages, valuation conventions, weights and product/service coverage can generate different movements. They are not three names for one universal inflation number.

The supplied articles attribute WPI/PPI releases to OEA under DPIIT and the consumer/industrial series to MoSPI. Keep the institution and index together, while verifying any newly claimed series and legal publication arrangements. A source calling a PPI series newly operative is not enough to establish that its coverage or base is official.

Invented fuel-price shock raises wholesale input costs sharply while retail prices adjust more slowly because taxes, margins and contracts differ. WPI and CPI can diverge without one necessarily being wrong. A fall in wholesale inflation does not guarantee immediate retail deflation, and CPI can move because of services not mirrored in the wholesale-goods basket.

For FM/ESI, explain pass-through with lags and incomplete transmission. Do not assume all producer prices are consumer prices or that a higher index number across different bases means a higher living cost. Learn scope, basket and purpose before memorising the monthly figure. Comparisons are meaningful only when units and the series definitions are respected.

teaching_notes.title: 3. Weighted contribution, food inflation and rural/urban comparison
paragraphs: An aggregate index combines components with weights under its methodology. A component with the fastest price increase does not necessarily contribute the most to overall inflation. Contribution depends on its weight and the calculation method as well as its own change. Simply averaging all listed component rates is generally incorrect.

In a simplified invented fixed-weight example, food has weight 40% and annual inflation 10%, while the rest has weight 60% and inflation 2%. The weighted rate is 0.4 x 10 + 0.6 x 2 = 5.2%. This is a teaching approximation with explicit assumptions, not a reconstruction of an official release.

Rural and urban baskets and aggregation weights differ. A combined rate is not necessarily the arithmetic mean of rural and urban rates. Food inflation, housing/rental measures and headline inflation also describe different subsets or aggregates. A high item-level rate, such as a vegetable spike, should not be substituted for household inflation as a whole.

The file's state and item rankings are selected-source observations with stated population/reference conditions, not universal rankings for every resident or period. Study the condition and interpretation; do not spend more time on every item ranking than on weighted contributions. For descriptive answers, explain distributional exposure: households buying different baskets experience different pressures even when the headline index is the same.

teaching_notes.title: 4. Base effects, rebasing and provisional/final estimates
paragraphs: A base effect changes a growth rate because the comparison-period level is unusual. Rebasing changes a series' reference framework and may also update weights, methods or coverage. These are different ideas. Prices can rise this month while annual inflation falls if the year-earlier comparison changes sufficiently.

Invented current index is 120. Compared with 100 a year earlier, growth is 20%; compared with 115, it is about 4.35%. The current level is identical in both comparisons. A lower annual rate does not necessarily mean current prices fell, and disinflation is not the same as deflation.

Provisional estimates use available information and may be revised as responses or corrections arrive. A weighted response rate indicates the information available under its compilation method, not the percentage of households whose inflation is exactly measured or a probability that the result is true. Final status does not mean impossible to revise under every statistical policy.

The October file claims new CPI and WPI/PPI bases and expanded IIP coverage. Those details are on verification hold. Do not splice a reported new-series index into an older series without an official linking/comparability method. Preserve release vintage, reference period, base, units and status. Revisions should be recorded as dated observations rather than silently overwriting the old value.

teaching_notes.title: 5. IIP: production volume, sectors and use-based groups
paragraphs: IIP tracks industrial production volume under its defined basket and weights. It is not the same as nominal sales, wholesale prices or the economy's entire GDP. Services and agriculture are not automatically represented simply because they use industrial products. Coverage must come from the applicable official series, not a guessed list.

Sectoral classification groups activity by industry. Use-based classification groups products by economic purpose, such as capital goods, intermediate inputs and consumer goods. The two classifications answer different questions. A machine used to produce other goods is capital goods; a component consumed in production can be intermediate goods. Consumer durables and non-durables differ in service life/use.

Invented current IIP is 123 and the year-earlier value is 114. Growth is about 7.89%, not 23%. Rapid capital-goods production can suggest stronger investment-related activity, but orders, imports, inventories and base effects matter. It does not establish that all private investment has already increased by the same rate.

The file reports additional sectors and a new base that have not been independently authenticated. Do not learn that expanded coverage as settled fact. For interpretation, compare weighted contributions and breadth rather than only the fastest sector. A small sector's very high growth may contribute less than moderate manufacturing growth in a much larger weighted segment.

teaching_notes.title: 6. Reading the October releases without false precision
paragraphs: For each retained statistic, record indicator, publisher, reference period, series/base and revision status. Add units and source vintage when needed. This makes later monthly updates appendable rather than turning a notes page into a collection of contradictory 'latest' figures. The edition month is metadata, not necessarily the month measured.

The file reports WPI annual inflation of 9.92% for August and 11.39% for September. The difference is 1.47 percentage points. It separately reports an index increase from 110.8 to 112.5: 1.7 index points, or about 1.53% month-on-month under comparability assumptions. These are source-data calculations, not authenticated observations or the same statistic.

The policy narrative rounds August CPI to 4.8% while a table gives 4.83%. That can be rounding rather than a genuine conflict. In contrast, a different base or different provisional/final status may explain a more substantive difference. Investigate definitions before declaring one value false or combining them.

The goal is not to memorise every decimal in a long release. Master the headline with its scope, a small set of important drivers and one interpretive takeaway after verification. Retain uncertainty explicitly where the source is doubtful. For descriptive answers, use verified data sparingly to support a mechanism; more unverified numbers do not make an answer more analytical.

teaching_notes.title: 1. Fiscal, revenue and primary deficit
paragraphs: Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus the relevant non-debt receipts under the accounting framework. It represents the financing gap rather than a measure of every type of government debt outstanding. Including borrowing on the receipts side and then declaring the deficit zero would confuse financing with income.

Revenue deficit compares revenue expenditure with revenue receipts. Primary deficit subtracts interest payments from fiscal deficit. These answer different questions: the overall financing requirement, imbalance on the revenue account and the deficit excluding the interest burden. A lower primary deficit does not mean all debt-service obligations disappear.

Invented government spends Rs 100, receives Rs 70 revenue receipts and Rs 5 non-debt capital receipts, and pays Rs 10 interest included in spending. Fiscal deficit is Rs 25; primary deficit is Rs 15. If revenue expenditure is Rs 80, revenue deficit is Rs 10. Borrowing finances the gap; it is not added as ordinary revenue to eliminate it.

Fiscal policy can support demand and productive capacity, but debt sustainability depends on growth, interest costs, future primary balances and risk. Avoid judging a deficit only as 'good' or 'bad'. Explain size, composition, cycle and financing. The October observation is a partial-year source claim and cannot by itself determine the full-year outcome or sustainability.

teaching_notes.title: 2. Receipts and expenditure: revenue/capital classifications
paragraphs: Tax revenue comes from imposed taxes; non-tax revenue can include specified fees, dividends and other receipts under budget classification. Non-debt capital receipts include relevant recoveries or asset-related transactions that are not new borrowing. Net tax receipts and gross tax collections differ where transfers or other adjustments apply, so preserve the accounting scope.

Revenue expenditure generally covers recurring operations and transfers in its classified form; capital expenditure includes spending classified as asset creation/acquisition or liability reduction under the accounts. Classification is not a perfect measure of social value. Education or health spending can improve future productivity while being classified as revenue expenditure, and a poorly designed capital project can produce little benefit.

Invented budget spends more on a road but cuts maintenance and teacher availability. A higher capital-expenditure share alone does not establish better outcomes. Evaluation needs project quality, complementary operating services, execution and distribution. Conversely, routine spending is not automatically wasteful just because it does not create a directly recorded physical asset.

In the October tables, component receipts and the headline total do not reconcile exactly at the displayed precision. Do not silently force the numbers to match. Record the discrepancy and seek the underlying accounts before precise decomposition. The supplied Budget note provides context for budget estimates, not independent official authentication of the monthly compilation.

teaching_notes.title: 3. Annual target, GDP ratio and half-year progress
paragraphs: A percentage of the annual deficit target is not a percentage of GDP. The first denominator is the budgeted financing gap; the second is the economy's output measure. A debt-to-GDP ratio uses a stock of debt, while a fiscal-deficit-to-GDP ratio uses a period's financing gap. Substituting these measures can reverse the meaning of a news report.

Using the compilation's unverified numbers as arithmetic material, Rs 7.14 lakh crore divided by an Rs 16.96 lakh crore annual target is about 42.1%. It does not mean the deficit is 42.1% of GDP or that the annual target has already been exceeded. The separate 4.3%-of-GDP target has a different denominator.

Half-year revenue and expenditure are seasonal. Tax due dates, transfers, dividends and project execution can bunch in particular months. Doubling a six-month deficit is not a justified forecast unless the assumptions support that projection. A year-on-year change in progress against BE may also reflect a changed annual target, not only the amount spent.

The displayed subtraction 25.50 minus 18.35 gives 7.15, while the source headline says 7.14; receipt components total 18.36. Possible rounding or scope differences are not a licence to invent a reconciliation. Learn the identity, preserve the unresolved precision gap and use authentic CGA accounts before presenting an exact factual analysis.

teaching_notes.title: 4. Windfall tax, export incentives and domestic prices
paragraphs: A windfall tax seeks to capture part of exceptional gains associated with unusual conditions. In petroleum, the relevant policy can be structured through a specific levy on designated products or activities. The legal tax base matters: an export levy, a domestic excise change and a tax on profits are not interchangeable just because all are described as windfall-related.

If export margins rise, refiners may prefer overseas sales. A levy can reduce that incentive and raise revenue, but also affects margins and supply responses. Its impact depends on global prices, refining costs, exchange rates and domestic arrangements. Reducing the levy can support exporter margins without compelling an equal reduction in domestic retail prices.

Invented export levy falls from Rs 10 to Rs 7 per litre on a qualifying product. The direct tax reduction is Rs 3 per litre exported. That is not automatically Rs 3 off every domestic pump transaction. The economic incidence can also be shared through prices, margins or quantities rather than falling exclusively on the legally liable exporter.

The October diesel/ATF rates, historical introduction date and unchanged petrol treatment remain unverified. Learn the product-scope and incidence logic instead of merging every petroleum tax into one rate. For an ESI/FM answer, discuss revenue, domestic availability, incentives and policy predictability; acknowledge that frequent revisions can help adapt to volatility while adding business uncertainty.

teaching_notes.title: 5. T-bills, fixed/floating bonds, SDLs and tax claims
paragraphs: Treasury bills are short-term central-government instruments conventionally issued at a discount and redeemed at face value. Fixed-rate bonds have a specified coupon structure; floating-rate coupons reset using a benchmark under their terms. State Development Loans are state-government securities. 'Government security' does not mean every holder faces identical tax treatment or market risk.

Invented T-bill is bought for Rs 98 and redeemed at Rs 100. The Rs 2 difference is a return over its holding period, not automatically a 2% annual yield regardless of tenor. A fixed-rate G-Sec can fall in market price when yields rise. A floating-rate structure changes rate exposure but does not remove every price, liquidity or reset risk.

A substantive tax exemption defines eligible persons, instruments and income. A declaration form specifies the evidence/procedure for a claim. A form does not by itself create a universal exemption for all investors. Interest income and a capital gain on sale also represent different income categories and may have different treatment.

The file's Form 173A, Rule 281A, ordinance, eligible FII/BIS categories and commencement claims are on verification hold. Do not use them for tax advice or memorise that all G-Sec income is exempt. For the exam, learn issuer/cash-flow distinctions and eligibility -> income -> instrument -> legal basis -> procedure. In this tax article BIS refers to the Bank for International Settlements, not the Bureau of Indian Standards involved in sorting-machine standards.
